_meta.status: PROPOSED — labels are authored by the coding agent and await human review. Not human-approved.
_meta.purpose: Fixed semantic evaluation set for the debate-progress judge. Each case gives the prior history, the pair under judgement, and the expected per-side labels. The judge is correct on a case when its new_evidence and first_reply flags match the expected flags for both sides, and its outcome matches the expected outcome.

fields.history: the debate history before the pair under judgement (speaker-labelled turns)
fields.bull_turn: the bull turn of the pair under judgement
fields.bear_turn: the bear turn of the pair under judgement
fields.expect_bull: expected {new_evidence, first_reply} for the bull turn, judged against history
fields.expect_bear: expected {new_evidence, first_reply} for the bear turn, judged against history plus the bull turn

cases.history: Bull Analyst: Revenue grew by 10% this year.
cases.bull_turn: Bull Analyst: Gross margin was 10% and holding.
cases.bear_turn: Bear Analyst: A 10% gross margin is thin for this sector.
cases.rationale: The number 10 is reused, but gross margin is a different fact from revenue growth; both sides introduce new evidence.

cases.history:
Bull Analyst: Revenue grew 10%.
Bear Analyst: Valuation is stretched.
cases.bull_turn: Bull Analyst: Management signalled a durable competitive moat from its new brand partnerships.
cases.bear_turn: Bear Analyst: Brand partnerships can be terminated at will, so they are fragile.
cases.rationale: A new qualitative fact with no number, entity, or ID is still new evidence.

cases.history:
Bull Analyst: Revenue grew 10% [FUN-01].
Bear Analyst: Valuation is stretched [MKT-02].
cases.rationale: Only the citation labels changed; the facts and rebuttals are repeats.

cases.history:
Bull Analyst: Margins are expanding.
Bear Analyst: Rising input costs will compress margins.
cases.bull_turn: Bull Analyst: Input-cost contracts are fixed through next year, so the compression the bear expects will not occur.
cases.bear_turn: Bear Analyst: Fixed contracts expire, leaving exposure after year end.
cases.rationale: The bull's turn is a first substantive reply to the bear's unanswered margin-compression point, with no explicit reply marker; the bear then replies first to the bull's contract point.

cases.history:
Bull Analyst: Growth is durable.
Bear Analyst: To address growth, I note demand is cyclical.
Bull Analyst: Demand is not cyclical because backlog is multi-year.
Bear Analyst: To address your backlog point, the backlog can be cancelled.
cases.bull_turn: Bull Analyst: Regarding your demand point, demand is not cyclical because backlog is multi-year.
cases.bear_turn: Bear Analyst: To address your backlog point, the backlog can be cancelled.
cases.rationale: Both turns carry reply markers but each merely re-asserts a rebuttal already made and answered earlier; neither side introduces evidence or a first reply to a still-unanswered point.

cases.history:
Bull Analyst: Growth is durable.
Bear Analyst: To address growth, I note demand is cyclical.
Bull Analyst: Demand is not cyclical because backlog is multi-year.
cases.bull_turn: Bull Analyst: Regarding your demand point, demand is not cyclical because backlog is multi-year.
cases.bear_turn: Bear Analyst: To address your backlog point: multi-year backlog does not refute cyclical demand; demand is cyclical regardless of how long the backlog runs.
cases.rationale: The bull repeats its earlier backlog rebuttal behind a marker (no progress). The bear's turn gives its first substantive response to that backlog point, using only already-known facts (multi-year backlog, cyclical demand) and introducing no new evidence; the first reply alone is progress.

cases.history_a:
Bear Analyst: Demand is cyclical.
Bull Analyst: Backlog is multi-year, so demand is insulated.
cases.history_b:
Bear Analyst: Demand is cyclical.
Bull Analyst: Backlog is multi-year, so demand is insulated.
Bear Analyst: Backlog can be cancelled.
cases.reply_text: Bull Analyst: Backlog is multi-year, so demand is insulated.
cases.rationale: The identical reply is a first response in history A (the bear's cyclicality point was unanswered) and a repeat in history B (already answered).
